### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-mcp`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `12e069ca1a1460f58b8be4191dcdf04e62e836b5` — the merge of head `8b24dd6d99a3a5b831826b4365d9253bfb7c0240` into base `b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 12e069ca1a1460f58b8be4191dcdf04e62e836b5 && git checkout 12e069ca1a1460f58b8be4191dcdf04e62e836b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372 8b24dd6d99a3a5b831826b4365d9253bfb7c0240 && git checkout -B drift-repro b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372 && git merge --no-ff 8b24dd6d99a3a5b831826b4365d9253bfb7c0240

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b4ccbc6f1052090751489741247deae55b726372` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inputs: card #27429 (body: the five texts, the seat's claim and its amendment adding the materializer docblock as a sixth), PR #28346 (body, the file list of 6 files, the diff of 74 changed lines against `main`, the two commits from the merge-base 501c864d), the 54 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T06:18Z: all 54 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test UI (matrix shard/16), UI Published Artifacts), and the tree on `main` for the rule each text now states: `plugin.ts` (the reconcile's `resolveConnectorCredential` call and its `catch` at :2336 to :2348, `degradeConnectorForCredential` at :2815 to :2860, `clearConnectorCredential` at :3056 to :3075) and `connector-credentials.ts` (`ConnectorCredentialUnavailableError` at :147, `missingCredentialReason` at :515). The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); `main` moved `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` since the merge-base (#28331, a different section) and the merge is clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The ADR-0097 amendment note states the code's rule, fact by fact** - right. A reference no source answers for (`resolution.kind` is `missing`) degrades the instance at boot and on a reload through the same door, and a live connector under that name is dematerialized first ("its credential is no longer set"); a stored credential the deployment cannot read now (any other non-resolved kind) degrades too and the warn line says the previously materialized connector keeps serving; both land in `degradedInstances` for the backoff; a host resolver that throws goes through `fail`, which is fatal at boot and logged and skipped on a reload. The "Upstream availability" pointer and the header's `Amended by` entry follow the ADR's own amendment style (#27237 and #28038 entries already sit on that line).
- **`clearConnectorCredential`'s contract gains the `503`** - right. The door throws `ConnectorCredentialUnavailableError` (status `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE_STATUS`, the door's 503) when the store's clear throws, and the walled-posture refusal sits before it; "nothing is changed" is true because the throw precedes any write. The interface docblock is the contract authors and the OpenAPI read, so this is the right place.
- **The connectors page, the MCP provider comment and the materializer docblock** - right. The example's comment now says the reference resolves at materialization and an unset one degrades; the MCP factory never sees an unresolvable reference because the materializer `continue`s after degrading before any factory call; the docblock's fatal list keeps the host-resolver throw and drops the unresolvable reference, naming the door.
- **The QA item follows the degrade rule and bumps its revision** - right. `acceptance[2]` becomes an `api` clause (the degraded descriptor, the warn line, the dispatch failure), `negative[2]` fails a boot that dies on it, `fixtures.requires[2]` names the env, store, host chain, `steps` and `refs` name the door test and the materialization test's current case name, and a `revision: 5` history entry cites #27429. `check:platform-checklist` stays off per-PR CI by standing decision (`fleet-patrols.yml`), so the dev's local run is the evidence for the checklist's shape; the QA file is text, not a gate input for landing.
- **Accept-set: nothing moves** - right. Comments, docs and a QA JSON only; no schema, export or runtime path. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right; `skip-changeset` is right for a diff that ships no package bytes (the `automation-service.ts` change is a docblock in the spec contract source, which the built package carries, but the lane's precedent for comment-only contract edits is no entry).
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **No release; `skip-changeset`** - accepted as above.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H by `docs/adr/**`** - os-zhuang approves after the seat's ACCEPT; the seat lands.
- **Serial overlap with #28317 on `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`** - #28317 (ADR-0143 S1) edits the same page in other sections and is dirty against `main` already; whichever lands second merges `main`. No shared hunk.
- **The 503 docblock names two causes the door raises from two places** - the store's clear throwing (read here) and the tenancy posture being unreadable (raised inside `doorCredentialChain`, not re-read line by line here; the dev measured it). Not owed.
- **Out of scope, left alone** - the connectors page's wider "boot fatal" vocabulary elsewhere on the page was not re-audited beyond the hunk the card named.

**Verdict reasoning.** Six texts now state the rule the code has had since #27237, each checked against the door on `main`; nothing runtime moves; the ADR edit is a dated amendment in the record's own style; every check is green or skipped and the head is clean against `main`.
